answer: Quadratic cost scaling at the identity registry: each new ID locks stake proportional to n². An echo of prior registrations is cheap to detect, so duplicates raise no benefit. The harbor enforces a per-epoch fee that doubles every tier. To farm 100 identities an attacker locks 10,000× the base stake, far exceeding the pearl of one verified seat. Break-even never arrives; cost outruns reward by 50×.
